sentences.text:
Hon'ble Ajay Bhanot,J.
Learned A.G.A contends that no instructions have been forthcoming from the police authorities.
Liberty of citizens is too sacrosanct and cannot be held to ransom by apathy of the police officials.
There is no cause for failing to provide instructions to the learned Government Advocate despite advance notice of the bail application.

By means of the the bail application the applicants have prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No. 186 of 2024 at Police Station- Rani Ki Sarai, District- Azamgarh under Sections 498A, 304 B IPC & 3/4 D.P. Act.
The applicant is in jail since 28.06.2024.

sentences.text: The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 26.03.2025

The following arguments made byJanardan Yadav, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Sri Chandan Agrawal, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The applicant is the husband of the deceased.
2. The applicant did not torture the deceased nor demanded dowry.
In fact the relations between the applicant and the deceased were harmonious.
3. The deceased was suffering from a chronic ailment.
The applicant was ensuring that best medical care was provided to the deceased.
The deceased died of the aforesaid ailment.
4. The details of the medical treatment afforded by the applicant to the victim and the bills are appended to the bail application.
5. The postmortem report opines the cause of death could not be ascertained.
The postmortem report do not depict any injury to the body of the deceased.
6. The FIR was registered at the instigation of inimical parties to blackmail the applicant and extort money from him.
7. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from the instant case.
8. The applicant is not flight risk.
The applicant being law abiding citizen have always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of their influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.
Let the applicant- Sagar @ Raj be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.

The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
( ii )
The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.
